t: Historians widely agree that preserving slavery was the principal aim of secession, as the states' own secession documents show; in 1860 enslaved people were 39 per cent of the eleven states' population and 31 per cent of free households owned slaves.

Its permanent constitution copied much of the United States Constitution verbatim but added explicit protections for slavery in every territory, forbade any state to bar slaveholders from bringing their slaves in, and kept the ban on the African slave trade.

Outnumbered about four to one in military manpower and far more in industry and railroads, the Confederacy passed the first national conscription in North America on 16 April 1862, financed itself by printing money until flour cost $100 a barrel in Richmond, and won recognition from no foreign government.
dyk: No foreign government ever recognised the Confederacy: when Ambrose Dudley Mann reported a letter from Pope Pius IX addressed to "the Illustrious and Honorable Jefferson Davis, President of the Confederate States of America", Secretary of State Judah P. Benjamin replied that Mann had mistranslated it and that it was "a mere inferential recognition".
ev: On 20 December South Carolina votes unanimously for secession after Abraham Lincoln's election; Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana and Texas follow by 1 February 1861.
On 8 February delegates at the Montgomery Convention form the Confederate States of America; Jefferson Davis is elected provisional president the next day.
On 12 April Confederate forces under Beauregard bombard and take Fort Sumter in Charleston harbor; Lincoln calls up 75,000 militia and Virginia, Arkansas, Tennessee and North Carolina secede.
Davis is inaugurated under the permanent constitution for a six-year term; the Permanent Congress has opened in Richmond on 18 February.
On 16 April the Confederate Congress imposes the first mass conscription on North American territory, making white men from 18 to 35 soldiers for three years.
Lee's invasion of Maryland is turned back at Antietam and Bragg's of Kentucky fails; Lincoln's preliminary Emancipation Proclamation ends British and French thoughts of recognition.
Vicksburg and Port Hudson fall, closing the Mississippi, and Lee's strike into Pennsylvania is repulsed at Gettysburg; the Confederacy withdraws into an interior defence.
On 9 April Richmond having fallen when Lee's lines broke at Petersburg, Lee surrenders at Appomattox Court House; Davis is captured on 10 May and the last land forces surrender by June.

f.capital: Montgomery, Alabama (4 February – 29 May 1861); Richmond, Virginia (from 30 May 1861); Danville for eight days in April 1865
f.founder: The Montgomery Convention of the seceded Deep South states, 4–8 February 1861; Jefferson Davis, provisional and then permanent president
f.predecessor: Seven slave states of the United States that passed secession ordinances between 20 December 1860 and 1 February 1861, joined by four more after Fort Sumter
f.successor: The United States, which readmitted the states to Congress during Reconstruction after each ratified the Thirteenth Amendment
